title: Irrigation Water Depth Calculator
description: Convert irrigation volume or flow into applied water depth with the Irrigation Water Depth Calculator — acre-inches and gallons reconciled. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, 100,000 gallons spread over 2 acres is 1.84 inches of water — the acre-inch (27,154 gallons) is the exchange rate that turns a pump log into a depth.
quick_answer: The Irrigation Water Depth Calculator converts a volume of water, or a flow rate over time, into the depth it applies across a field — inches of water over acres. Enter the gallons (or flow and hours) and field size and read the applied depth.

use_cases.title: Checking a water bill or allocation

body.t: Districts allocate in acre-feet; fields drink in inches. One acre-foot is 325,851 gallons — twelve acre-inches stacked — and this page converts allocations into per-field depths.
Two fields, one pump log: depths expose which field was actually watered and which was merely visited. Field areas come from the
when the acreage is a rumour.
A storm drops 0.8 inches — what would the pump have charged for that? At 27,154 gallons per acre-inch, an inch over 10 acres is 271,543 gallons of free water, priced.
One acre covered one inch deep holds 27,154 gallons (43,560 sq ft × 1/12 ft × 7.48052 gal/ft³). Every irrigation conversion on this page is that single number wearing different clothes.
500 gpm × 600 minutes = 300,000 gallons. Over 5 acres: 300,000 ÷ 27,154 ÷ 5 = 2.21 inches. Three multiplications turn a flow gauge into a soil-moisture decision.

popular_table.title: Water depth exchange rates
popular_table.intro: The constants this calculator lives by — all derived from the acre-inch.
popular_table.note: Depths are gross applied water. What the crop keeps depends on system efficiency — sprinklers lose some to wind and evaporation, drip loses least; the calculator prices the application, the agronomist prices the loss.

faq: Does it account for irrigation efficiency?

The computed depth is water applied at the field. Effective depth in the root zone is lower — multiply by your system's efficiency (drip often 90%+, sprinklers 75–85%, flood lower) for the scheduling figure.
Flow rate instead of a total volume?
Multiply flow by run time first (gallons per minute × minutes) — or enter flow and hours where the tool offers it; the depth comes from the total volume either way.
Use the actually-irrigated acres, not the field's deed acres. A pivot watering 120 of 130 acres concentrates its volume — depth rises accordingly, and corners stay dry by design.
Rain gauges already report depth — one inch of rain on one acre equals one acre-inch, 27,154 gallons you did not pump. Comparing the two is the budgeting habit this page encourages.
Hectares and litres convert through the same physics: one inch over one hectare is 102,790 litres (a millimetre over a hectare is 10,000 litres — the metric system's tidier proverb).
That is an agronomy question — soil type, crop stage and evapotranspiration decide it. This calculator's job is narrower: making sure the depth you intended is the depth you applied.
The arithmetic scales down untouched: 100 gallons over 500 sq ft is 0.32 inches. Depth is depth, at farm scale or flower-bed scale.
